repos.description: An LLM-powered knowledge curation system that researches a topic and generates a full-length report with citations.

paper.title: Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models

additional_papers.title: Into the Unknown Unknowns: Engaged Human Learning through Participation in Language Model Agent Conversations (Co-STORM)

repos.what_it_does: Researches a topic by simulating conversations between perspective-specific question askers and a retrieval-grounded expert, turns the collected snippets into an outline, then writes a cited long-form article. Co-STORM (same package, knowledge-storm) adds a human-in-the-loop roundtable whose shared state is a dynamic mind map.
repos.what_to_borrow: Split pre-writing from writing: (1) perspective-guided question asking to enumerate what each section must cover, (2) an outline whose nodes carry the retrieved snippet IDs, (3) drafting where every sentence keeps pointers to those IDs so the evidence critic can re-verify them. Co-STORM's mind map is a good model for the shared blackboard that our 12 editor agents read and write.
repos.caveats: MIT code; FreshWiki data is CC BY-SA. Retrieval modules expect web-search API keys (we would plug in our own corpus retriever). Targets Wikipedia-style articles, not IMRaD papers. Push cadence has slowed (last push 2025-09-30).

repos.description: High accuracy RAG for answering questions from scientific documents with citations

paper.title: Language agents achieve superhuman synthesis of scientific knowledge (PaperQA2)

repos.what_it_does: Agentic RAG over local PDFs/text/code focused on scientific literature: paper search, chunk-level evidence gathering with relevance scoring and contextual summaries, and answers with in-text citations; enriches documents with metadata (citation counts, retraction checks, licences) from scholarly APIs.
repos.what_to_borrow: Use its 'gather evidence -> summarize each chunk relative to the claim with a score -> answer only from top-scored evidence -> say 'cannot answer' when evidence is thin' contract as the writer's rule set. Copy the idea of a metadata-enrichment step with a retraction check before any paper enters our citable corpus.
repos.caveats: Apache-2.0, actively maintained. Many LLM calls per answer (cost/latency); defaults route through LiteLLM to hosted models; some metadata providers need API keys.

repos.description: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery 🧑‍🔬
repos.license_detail: The AI Scientist Source Code License v1.0 (Dec 2025), derived from the Responsible AI Source Code License (use-based restrictions). GitHub reports NOASSERTION.

paper.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery

repos.what_it_does: End-to-end system that proposes ideas, runs experiments from code templates, writes a LaTeX paper section by section with literature search for citations, and grades the result with an automated reviewer modelled on conference review forms.
repos.what_to_borrow: Section-by-section LaTeX drafting with a fixed number of self-reflection rounds per section, a compile-and-repair loop for LaTeX errors, and an ensemble LLM reviewer (several reviews + meta-review) as a template for our judge agent.
repos.caveats: Custom RAIL-derived licence, not OSI-approved; read its use restrictions before reusing code or prompts. Executes LLM-written code (must be sandboxed). Templates are small ML domains, so prose quality is not its focus.

paper.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search

repos.what_it_does: Template-free successor that explores experiments with a progressive agentic tree search run by an experiment-manager agent and writes the manuscript; the README reports a fully AI-written paper accepted at an ICLR 2025 workshop through peer review.
repos.what_to_borrow: Its best-first tree search over alternatives (parameters in bfts_config.yaml) suggests keeping several candidate drafts per section as tree nodes that the judge expands or prunes. The paper also reports vision-language-model feedback on figures, an idea for the evidence critic: check that caption, body text and plotted data agree.
repos.caveats: Same restrictive custom licence as v1; runs untrusted generated code; expensive; experiment automation, not writing quality, is the main contribution.

repos.what_it_does: Human-in-the-loop research workflow in which role-played agents (PhD student, postdoc, professor, ML engineer) handle literature review, planning, experiments and LaTeX report writing, with a co-pilot mode for human feedback at each phase.
repos.what_to_borrow: Explicit phases (literature review, experimentation, report writing) with co-pilot checkpoints where a human steers each phase; in our harness each transition (outline -> draft -> editing -> rebuttal) should be an author-approvable gate. The paper's iterative LaTeX report refinement scored by an LLM reviewer is a baseline for an 'accept an edit only if the judge score improves' protocol.
repos.caveats: MIT. Prompts and defaults target OpenAI/DeepSeek models; the writing module is basic; last push 2025-08-20.

Also useful: keeping implementation logs as structured evidence the writer must cite.

repos.what_to_borrow: Make data-chaining a hard rule: every number, comparison and percentage in a draft must link to an evidence record (results table cell, log line or cited-paper span), and the evidence critic rejects any unlinked number. Also borrow the rewind/replay of recorded runs and per-step cost tracking.

repos.what_to_borrow: The self-feedback loop (draft -> feedback -> extra retrieval -> revision -> final citation-verification pass that drops or repairs unsupported citations) maps one-to-one onto our writer <-> evidence-critic iteration. Its companion ScholarQABench (listed separately) gives ready-made citation metrics.
repos.caveats: Apache-2.0 code; checkpoints and datastore are large and their terms are set on Hugging Face (base-model licences apply); last push 2025-08-13.

repos.what_to_borrow: Planner -> parallel researchers -> report writer layout with source tracking per paragraph, and a 'local documents only' mode, which we would make mandatory so drafts can cite only our vetted corpus. The LangGraph multi-agent example is a compact reference for wiring role agents around shared state.
repos.caveats: Apache-2.0. Web scraping by default conflicts with our evidence-only-from-corpus rule; large dependency surface.

repos.what_to_borrow: Treat 'citation needed here' as an explicit decision: the writer emits a placeholder that must be resolved against our corpus (or the sentence is rewritten without the claim) before the paragraph is accepted. This prevents invented references by construction.
repos.caveats: MIT. Model and retrieval index are trained on arXiv CS papers; small community (few hundred stars).

repos.description: :pencil: A markup-aware linter for prose built with speed and extensibility in mind.

Run it before the LLM critics so they only see issues rules cannot catch, and feed its JSON output to the judge.

repos.description: A Vale-compatible implementation of the write-good linter.

repos.description: Style and Grammar Checker for 25+ Languages
repos.license_detail: LGPL-2.1-or-later (core).

repos.description: [Mirror] A linter for prose.

repos.description: textlint is the pluggable linter for natural language text.

repos.description: Spelling, grammar and style checking on LaTeX documents
repos.what_it_does: Spelling, grammar and style checker for LaTeX (and Markdown) that strips markup but keeps track of positions in the original file, sends the clear text to LanguageTool, and reports in console or HTML.
repos.what_to_borrow: The position-mapping trick is exactly what our editor needs: critics work on clean sentences, but every suggested edit must be mapped back to a line/column in the .tex source so it can be applied as a patch.
repos.caveats: GPL-3.0: call it as an external CLI rather than linking code. Java.

repos.description: LTeX+ Language Server: LSP language server for LanguageTool :mag::heavy_check_mark: with support for LaTeX :mortar_board:, Markdown :pencil:, and others
repos.what_it_does: Language server (LSP) that checks LaTeX, Markdown and other markup with LanguageTool; maintained continuation of LTeX LS.
repos.what_to_borrow: Author-facing editor integration: show our style-dictionary terms and false-positive lists in the author's editor via the LSP dictionary settings.

repos.description: Offline, privacy-first grammar checker. Fast, open-source, Rust-powered
repos.what_it_does: Private, offline English grammar checker that lints a document in milliseconds with a small memory footprint; available as a language server, JavaScript/WebAssembly package and editor plugins.
repos.what_to_borrow: Cheap regression check inside the agent loop: re-lint every proposed edit and reject edits that introduce new grammar errors, at negligible cost.
repos.caveats: Apache-2.0. English only; narrower coverage than LanguageTool.

repos.description: Stylometry library for Burrows' Delta method
repos.what_it_does: Python implementation of Burrows' Delta for authorship analysis, with probability calibration (probability that two texts share an author) and visualisation.
repos.what_to_borrow: Build function-word profiles per lab/author from the corpus and report the Delta distance between a draft and the target profile as a style-drift signal for the judge.
repos.caveats: MIT; small project. Delta needs reasonably long samples (thousands of words), so compute it per section or per paper, not per sentence.

repos.description: R package for stylometric analyses
repos.license_detail: GPL-3 per README; GitHub detects no licence file.
repos.what_it_does: R package for stylometric analysis: Delta-family distances, clustering, cross-validated classification (classify()), contrastive vocabulary analysis and rolling stylometry.
repos.what_to_borrow: Reference implementations to validate our Python stylometry, and rolling stylometry as a way to locate the passages where a draft's style shifts (e.g. paragraphs that read as generic LLM prose).
repos.caveats: R and GPL-3; use offline for analysis, not inside the product.

repos.description: Python package for stylometry
repos.license_detail: BSD-style licence file (copyright line names a different author). GitHub reports NOASSERTION.
repos.what_it_does: Early-stage Python toolkit for stylometry (corpus loading, vectorisation, dimensionality reduction, clustering) with API, CLI and browser GUI goals.
repos.what_to_borrow: Only its simple pipeline layout (corpus -> features -> reduction -> clustering) as a reference.
repos.caveats: Inactive since 2021-03-30 and self-described as early stage; prefer faststylometry or stylo.

repos.description: :memo: python package to calculate readability statistics of a text object - paragraphs, sentences, articles.
repos.what_it_does: Library of readability and text statistics (Flesch, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Dale-Chall, syllable and sentence counts and more).
repos.what_to_borrow: Compute per-section distributions (sentence length, readability) over accepted papers by the target lab and flag sentences in the tails for the concision agent; compare distributions, not absolute grade levels.

repos.description: :smile_cat: :speech_balloon: A module to compute textual lexical richness (aka lexical diversity).

repos.description: 💫 Industrial-strength Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Python
repos.what_it_does: Industrial-strength NLP library: tokenisation, sentence segmentation, POS tagging, dependency parsing, NER, rule matchers.
repos.what_to_borrow: Parser backbone for the linguistic agents: noun/reference (determiners, demonstratives such as bare 'this'), verb/modality (modal verbs, tense, voice), modifier/quantifier (adverbs, intensifiers, quantifier scope); encode style-dictionary patterns with Matcher/DependencyMatcher.
repos.caveats: MIT. General-domain models stumble on math and method names; combine with scispaCy or custom tokenizer rules.

repos.description: A full spaCy pipeline and models for scientific/biomedical documents.

repos.what_to_borrow: AbbreviationDetector for the terminology agent: every acronym defined once at first use, then used consistently; flag acronyms used before definition or redefined.

repos.description: Python Keyphrase Extraction module
repos.what_it_does: Python keyphrase-extraction toolkit implementing unsupervised (TextRank, TopicRank, MultipartiteRank, YAKE, ...) and supervised methods.

repos.description: Minimal keyword extraction with BERT
repos.what_it_does: Embedding-based keyword/keyphrase extraction with Max Sum Distance and Maximal Marginal Relevance diversification.

repos.description: Data for EMNLP 2022 paper "arXivEdits: Understanding the Human Revision Process in Scientific Writing".

repos.description: A package to evaluate factuality of long-form generation. Original implementation of our EMNLP 2023 paper "FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation"

repos.what_it_does: Splits long-form text into atomic facts and checks each against a knowledge source with retrieval plus an LM verifier, reporting the fraction supported; pip package with a configurable knowledge source.

repos.description: Supercharge Your LLM Application Evaluations 🚀

repos.description: Inspect: A framework for large language model evaluations
repos.what_it_does: UK AI Security Institute framework for LLM evaluations with components for prompting, tool use, multi-turn dialogue and model-graded scoring, plus 200+ prebuilt evaluations and a log viewer.

repos.description: Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs. Red teaming/pentesting/vulnerability scanning for AI. Compare performance of GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more. Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration.  Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.

repos.description: Benchmarking long-form factuality in large language models. Original code for our paper "Long-form factuality in large language models".

paper.title: Long-form factuality in large language models

repos.what_it_does: LongFact prompt set, SAFE (search-augmented factuality evaluator that splits a response into facts and verifies each with multi-step search) and the F1@K metric, with a pipeline for benchmarking OpenAI and Anthropic models.

repos.what_to_borrow: Extract only verifiable claims before checking them, so properly hedged or opinion sentences are not penalised; pairs naturally with the verb/modality agent that controls hedging.
repos.caveats: Apache-2.0. Needs a Serper API key for retrieval by default; small repo.

repos.what_to_borrow: Run a cheap local 'is this sentence supported by its cited passages?' check on every draft sentence and send only failures or borderline cases to the expensive LLM evidence critic.

Category 1 was split into research_writing_agents, peer_review_rebuttal and curated_lists; category 3 into prose_linting_stylometry and scientific_discourse_revision; category 6 into seven topic_* categories. scholarly_discovery is an added group covering harness stage (a), finding professors and accepted papers.

license is GitHub's spdx_id ('NOASSERTION' = GitHub could not classify the file; null = no licence file detected). license_detail is our reading of the LICENSE/README text and should be preferred where the two differ (e.g. microsoft/autogen code is MIT although GitHub reports CC-BY-4.0 for the docs licence).

paper.venue_source: 'readme' = taken from the repository README/BibTeX; 'repo_description' = from the GitHub description; 'prior_knowledge' = venue known from the literature but not re-verified in this session (the web-search budget ran out partway through), so recheck those before citing.

Suggested core stack from this map. Parsing: GROBID + Docling, with LaTeXML/ar5iv when arXiv sources exist. Discovery: openreview-py + pyalex + semanticscholar + arxiv.py, with paperlists/CSrankings for internal bootstrapping only. Deterministic style layer: Vale (+ write-good package) + LanguageTool + spaCy/scispaCy + textstat/LexicalRichness/faststylometry. Evidence checks: ALCE-style citation recall/precision, FActScore/SAFE-style atomic claims, MiniCheck/AlignScore as cheap local checkers, rebiber for bibliography hygiene. Evaluation harness: inspect_ai (+ promptfoo for prompt CI). Orchestration: LangGraph or the Claude Agent SDK, with instructor schemas and the anthropic / openai (AzureOpenAI) SDKs. Main design references: STORM, data-to-paper, Ai2 Scholar QA quote-first synthesis, OpenScholar self-feedback, DeepReviewer, AgentReview, DISAPERE, MAD/ChatEval, Self-Refine, TextGrad.

Calibration data for specific editor agents: meaning-preservation critic -> mitre/hpmet, AlignScore; judge -> JourdanL/parareval, PeerRead aspect scores; rebuttal agent -> DISAPERE, AgentReview, NLPeer; grammar/concision -> IteraTeR, CoEdIT, XtraGPT/ReviseQA; logic critic -> CSAbstruct, MuLMS-AZ zones; terminology -> scispaCy abbreviations, pke/KeyBERT term candidates; evidence critic -> SciFact record format, CiteME, ScholarQABench.
